g.text: The laws of reflection, refraction and wave optics are put to use in many instrumentsand technologies. Eight important applications are described below.
Convex lenses correctlong-sightedness and concavelenses correctshort-sightedness by bringingthe image exactly on to theretina. Contact lenses work onthe same principle of refraction.
A compound microscope usesan objective and an eyepiece togive a highly magnified image oftiny objects such as cells andbacteria. Its resolving power islimited by diffraction.
The objective collects lightfrom distant objects and theeyepiece magnifies the imageformed. Large reflectingtelescopes use concavemirrors to study planets, starsand galaxies.
A convex lens forms a real,inverted image on a film orelectronic sensor. The aperturecontrols the amount of light andthe shutter controls theexposure time.
Light travels along a thin glasscore by repeated total internalreflection. Fibres carrytelephone, television andinternet signals over longdistances with very little loss.
A laser gives an intense,monochromatic and coherentbeam. It is used in eye surgery,cutting and welding, barcodescanners, printers, optical discsand holography.
An endoscope uses bundles ofoptical fibres to carry light intothe body and bring the imageback, letting doctors examineinternal organs without majorsurgery.
Spectrometers, interferometersand polarimeters usedispersion, interference andpolarisation to measurewavelengths, tiny distancesand the concentration ofsolutions.
